entrypoint: PublicArgumentMCP.call_tool with the actual MCP server lifespan context
fixture: repository Fake X owned-process fixture; synthetic owner Display.sync block; patched cancellation callback held on a threading.Event
hypothesis: A pending standard-caller cancellation may keep graceful server lifespan shutdown blocked after owner.close returns because the cancellation executor is joined with wait=True.
measurement: Start server lifespan shutdown while the cancellation worker is held; observe owner.close return and whether lifespan exit completes before releasing the cancellation gate.

arms.reason: nested probe invocation did not add checkout root to sys.path

arms.qualification: os.kill(pid, 0) reported alive, but immediate Windows Get-Process found no such PID; do not use r02's owner-liveness field

arms.outcome: probe completed with Win32 process readback

limitations: one deterministic Windows Fake X construction run is not an X-server, physical-release, task-effect, reliability, or MAP01 result
the cancellation callback was test-gated before owner cancellation; it did not exercise XRes or a real blocked server request
the lifespan was entered through the in-process MCP server object; no stdio client or remote transport was exercised
the retained owner/session snapshot is stale relative to the post-shutdown Win32 PID readback
the observed delay is not a general shutdown deadline or process-termination guarantee
